notes: Stock example of yaṇ: i -> y before a following vowel. The first output (dadhyatra) is what 6.1.77 alone gives. daddhyatra is the Kāśikā's own example under 8.4.47 (quote: 'दद्ध्यत्र। मद्ध्वत्र।' on 8.4.47): 8.4.47 anaci ca doubles dh (dadhdhy atra) and 8.4.53 turns the first dh into d. dadhyyatra / daddhyyatra add the doubling of y by the vārttika 'yaṇo mayo dve' (Kāśikā on 8.4.47 reads it as 'दध्य्यत्र, मध्व्वत्रेत्युदाहरणम्'; Mahābhāṣya on 8.4.47 has 'दध्य्यत्र'). 8.2.23 saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ does NOT delete the final y of 'dadhy' because yaṇ is bahiraṅga and asiddha for it (Kāśikā on 8.2.23). Śākalya's optional prakṛtibhāva alternative 'dadhi atra' (6.1.127, other family) is deliberately not listed.

u -> v (1.1.50 sthānato 'ntaryāt: u is oṣṭhya, v is dantoṣṭhya, the nearest of y v r l). Kāśikā on 6.1.77 has plain मध्वत्र; on 8.4.47 it has मद्ध्वत्र (dh doubled, first dh -> d by 8.4.53); 'मध्व्वत्र' is the Kāśikā's example for the second reading of the vārttika 'yaṇo mayo dve' (v doubled after may). No saṃyogānta-lopa of the final v (yaṇ is asiddha as bahiraṅga for 8.2.23).
ṛ -> r. The Kāśikā lists only this form; optional 8.4.46 doubling of the t after r (karttrartham) is possible in principle but is not mentioned by the source.
Same pattern as kartrartham (ṛ -> r).

Compound ḷ-ākṛti ('the shape of ḷ'; Bālamanoramā on 8.2.23: 'ऌवर्णस्य आकृतिरिव आकृतिर्यस्य'). Split by me from the joined example. ḷ + ā are asavarṇa (ā is not ḷ-savarṇa), so yaṇ applies. Of y v r l the substitute is l (dantya, 1.1.50); Bālamanoramā on 8.2.23 explains why not v: both v and l are 'prāpta' and the later vidhi (l) wins by para-vipratiṣedha/apavāda. The Laghu text lists lākṛtiḥ as a vārttika example of 'yaṇaḥ pratiṣedho vācyaḥ' (no saṃyogānta-lopa; nothing to delete here anyway). Visarga is the nominative -s.

Vārttika 'यणादेशः प्लुतपूर्वस्य च' (Kāśikā: 'इकः प्लुतपूर्वस्य सवर्णदीर्घबाधनार्थं यणादेशो वक्तव्यः'): an ik that FOLLOWS a pluta vowel is turned into yaṇ although savarṇa-dīrgha (6.1.101) would otherwise apply. Written 'bho3 i indram' in the source; the project alphabet has no pluta digit, so the pluta is carried by flag 'pluta' on word 0 and omitted from the output. The lone 'i' is the pragṛhya nipāta i (Padamañjarī: 'इकारः स्वरादिपाठान्निपात प्रगृह्यसंज्ञकः'), whose prakṛtibhāva (6.1.125) is overridden by the yaṇ vārttika.
Mahābhāṣya example of the same vārttika ('अग्ना3इ इन्द्रम् - अग्ना3यिन्द्रम्'); I split the joined 'अग्ना3इ' into agnā(pluta) + i. Pluta digit omitted (no digit in the alphabet).
Mahābhāṣya example ('पटा3उ उदकम् - पटा3वुदकम्'); split by me into paṭā(pluta) + u + udakam.
Mahābhāṣya example ('अग्ना3इ आशा -अग्ना3याशा'); split by me.
Mahābhāṣya example ('पटा3उ आशा - पटा3वाशा'); split by me.
'aci iti kim?' (Nyāsa on 6.1.77): a following consonant gives no yaṇ.

'ik iti kim?' (Nyāsa): the consonant c is not replaced by a semivowel; kutva (8.2.30 coḥ kuḥ) alone gives the result. Kutva is the only rule the Nyāsa names; 8.2.39 (jhalāṃ jaśo 'nte) supplies the g and is added by me. Input written with underlying c (the source shows the result vāgatra).
Only the i BEFORE the vowel is replaced (tasmin nirdiṣṭe pūrvasya); the following u is untouched.
Same: u -> v, the following i stays.
i of pacati -> y before o.

Counter-example for the word 'nirdiṣṭa' (adjacency): the i of agnicit is separated from the vowel by the consonant c-t, so yaṇ cannot apply. The Mahābhāṣya on 6.1.77 says the same for the word 'ik' ('इह मा भूत् - अग्निचिदत्र, सोमसुदत्र । ... जश्त्वमत्र बाधकं भविष्यति'). The visible change t -> d is jaśtva (8.2.39), which the source names only in the Mahābhāṣya.

Counter-example for 'avyavahitasya' in 1.1.67 (Bālamanoramā: 'अव्यवहिते किम्, उत्प्रस्थानम् । उदःस्थास्तम्भोरिति पूर्वसवर्णो न भवति'): 8.4.61 udaḥ sthāstambhoḥ pūrvasya does not apply because the p of pra separates ud from sthā. The change d -> t before p is khari ca (8.4.55), not named by the source (my inference).
ci + lyuṭ -> ce + ana (guṇa) -> cayana; split by me from the joined example (Vasu: 'चि+ ल्युट् = चे + अन = चयनम्'); the final -m is the neuter nominative ending.
lū + lyuṭ -> lo + ana -> lavana (Vasu: 'लो + अन् = लवनं').
ci + ṇvul -> cai + aka (vṛddhi) -> cāyaka; visarga is the nominative -s.
lū + ṇvul -> lau + aka -> lāvaka.
Nyāsa on 6.1.78: 'के+एते'. ke is the nominative PLURAL of ka (not a dual, so no pragṛhya blocking). Shows e + e -> ay + e.
Nyāsa: 'ये+एत'. ye is the nominative plural of ya.
Nyāsa: 'वायौ+अवरुणद्धि'. au -> āv before a vowel. (The ṇ of avaruṇaddhi comes from 8.4.1, outside this family.)
Laghu text vlk_23 (yathāsaṃkhya): e -> ay, o -> av, ai -> āy, au -> āv in that order. hari + ṅe -> hare + e (guṇa) -> haraye; split by me from the joined form.
viṣṇu + ṅe -> viṣṇo + e -> viṣṇave. Split by me.
nī + ṇvul -> nai + aka -> nāyaka (ai -> āy). Split by me; visarga is the nominative -s.
pū + ṇvul -> pau + aka -> pāvaka (au -> āv). Split by me.

source.quote: hara iha, harayiha / viṣṇa iha, viṣṇaviha

notes: Laghu text vlk_31 (pūrvatrāsiddham): hare + iha -> haray + iha by 6.1.78 (sapādasaptādhyāyī, done first); then the tripādī rule lopaḥ śākalyasya (8.3.19: the y/v after a-varṇa at the end of a pada may be deleted before a vowel, optional) gives 'hara iha' (hiatus, written with a space) or, without deletion, 'harayiha'. This is the Laghu's own illustration of 8.2.1: 8.3.19 sees the output of 6.1.78.

source.quote: hara iha, harayiha / viṣṇa iha, viṣṇaviha

notes: Same as hare iha: viṣṇo + iha -> viṣṇav + iha -> viṣṇa iha / viṣṇaviha (o -> av).

go + yat (gopayasor yat, 4.3.160; Siddhāntakaumudī on 6.1.79 quotes this) -> gavya. o is not followed by a vowel so 6.1.78 cannot act; 6.1.79 supplies av before a y-initial affix. 'yam' = affix yat + neuter ending. Bālamanoramā: the following lopa rules 8.3.19/8.3.22 do not delete the v because the word is a bha here (no padatva).
nau + yat (nauvayodharmaviṣamūlamūlasītātulābhyas tāryatulyaprāpyavadhyānāmyasamasamitasaṃmiteṣu, 4.4.91) -> nāvya (au -> āv).

babhru + yañ -> bābhro + ya (ādivṛddhi + guṇa of u by 6.4.146) -> bābhravya. bābho is the post-guṇa stem (my split, following Vasu: 'बभ्रु + यञ् = बाभ्रो + य = बाभ्रव्यः'). The ya is a pratyaya; the stem is not a dhātu so 6.1.80 does not restrict it.
maṇḍu + yañ (gargādibhyo yañ, 4.1.105 per Nyāsa) -> māṇḍo + ya -> māṇḍavya. Split by me.
śaṅku + yat -> śaṅko + ya -> śaṅkavya (dāru 'wood'); split by me. The source prints the neuter ending as anusvāra before the next word (śaṅkavyaṃ dāru); the output here is the word in pause.
picu + yat -> pico + ya -> picavya (kārpāsa 'cotton'); split by me.
nau + yat -> nāvya; the source shows it in the phrase 'nāvyo hradaḥ' (visarga -> o before the voiced h, another family).

'vānta iti kim?': ai is not replaced by āv (only o/au take the va-ending replacements). rai + kyac -> raiyati ('desires wealth'). Padamañjarī: the word rai is Vedic-only ('रैशब्दश्छान्दसः'). Input splits the kyac-verb form as rai + yati (my split).

Mahābhāṣya: without the word 'vānta' 6.1.79 would turn e before ya into ay in ceyam/jeyam; the actual forms keep e. Meaning: ci + yat 'to be collected/fit to be collected' (not śakya-arthe, so 6.1.81 does not apply).
'yi iti kim?': the affix does not begin with y, so no av.
Same: bh-initial ending.
'pratyaya iti kim?': yāna is a word (ṣaṣṭhī-samāsa), not a pratyaya beginning with y.
Same as goyānam.
Vārttika 'गोर्यूतौ छन्दस्युपसंख्यानम्' (Vedic): go before yūti -> gav-yūti (ṚV 3.62.16 'आ नो मित्रावरुणा ... गव्यूतिमुक्षतम्'). yūti is not a pratyaya, hence the vārttika. Split by me.

SEMANTIC-CONDITION (not decidable from the letters alone): vārttika 'adhvaparimāṇe ca' (the Laghu text spells it 'adhvaparamāṇe ci'): go before yūti -> gavyūtiḥ (a measure of road, krośa-yuga) also in the ordinary language. Same letters as the counter-example goyūtiḥ. yūti is nipātita (SK: ऊतियूतिजूतिसातिहेतिकीर्तयश्च).
SEMANTIC-CONDITION (not decidable from the letters alone): 'chandasīti kim?': outside the Veda (and outside the measure-of-road sense) the word stays goyūtiḥ.

derivation.note: guṇa of ū, conditioned by the y-affix (source: Bālamanoramā on 6.1.80)
o -> av before a y-initial pratyaya; 6.1.80 allows it because this o was made by that very affix

notes: lū + yat -> lo + ya (guṇa by 7.3.84, produced BY the y-affix) -> lavya. Bālamanoramā spells the steps: 'अचो यत् । सार्वधातुकार्धधातुकयोरित्यूकारस्य गुण ओकारः । तस्य धात्ववयवत्वाद्यादिप्रत्ययानिमित्तकत्वाच्च वान्तादेशः'. Input is the root + affix before guṇa; 'yam' = yat + neuter ending. Split by me.
Same as lavyam (pū + yat).

lū + ṇyat (orāvaśyake 3.1.125): the ū gets vṛddhi au (aco ñṇiti 7.2.115, named by Nyāsa), again produced by the affix, so au -> āv. The compound with avaśyam (mayūravyaṃsakādi, m dropped: Nyāsa 'लुम्पेदवश्यमः कृत्ये') is spelled out by me as avaśya + lau + yam.

Counter-example for 'tannimittasya': Nyāsa derives upoyate from ā/upa + ve + yak -> ūyate; the guṇa o comes from upa + ū (ādguṇaḥ 6.1.87), NOT from the y-affix, so 6.1.79 must not turn it into av. The inner u -> ū (7.4.25) is caused by yak; the o is not. Split by me from the Nyāsa's description.

Counter-example: lūyamāna + iñ (ata iñ 4.1.95) with vṛddhi au by taddhiteṣv acām ādeḥ 7.2.117 (Nyāsa: 'सा च तद्धितनिमित्ता, न तु यकारादिप्रत्ययनिमित्ता'); au is not caused by the y-affix, so no āv. pauyamāniḥ is the twin example.

SEMANTIC-CONDITION (not decidable from the letters alone): nipātana: e of kṣi (+yat) becomes ay only in the sense 'able to be' (śakyaḥ kṣetuṃ kṣayyaḥ). kṣe = guṇa-ed kṣi. Same letters would give kṣeyam in the 'fit to be' sense.
SEMANTIC-CONDITION (not decidable from the letters alone): śakyo jetuṃ jayyaḥ.
SEMANTIC-CONDITION (not decidable from the letters alone): 'śakyārtha iti kim?': in the sense 'fit/worthy to be destroyed' (arhe kṛtyatṛcaś ca, 3.3.169) the e stays: kṣeyaṃ pāpam.
SEMANTIC-CONDITION (not decidable from the letters alone): Siddhāntakaumudī's counter-example (Kāśikā has 'जेयो वृषलः'): jeyam manaḥ 'the mind is to be conquered' (yogya, not śakya).
SEMANTIC-CONDITION (not decidable from the letters alone): nipātana: krī + yat -> krayya only when the thing is 'put out for sale' (tadarthe: krayārthaṃ yaḥ prasāritaḥ). kre = guṇa-ed krī.

SEMANTIC-CONDITION (not decidable from the letters alone): 'tadartha iti kim?': 'kreyaṃ no dhānyam, na cāsti krayyam' — grain we want to buy is kreya (kre-ya, e stays); only grain put out for sale is krayya.
Vedic nipātana: bhī + yat (kṛtyalyuṭo bahulam, 3.3.113, ablative sense: 'that from which one is afraid') -> bhayya. bhe = guṇa-ed bhī.
Vedic nipātana in the feminine only (Kāśikā: 'प्रवय्या इति स्त्रियामेव निपातनम्। अन्यत्र प्रवेयमित्येव भवति'): pra + vī + yat + āp. Split by me.

Vārttika 'हृदय्या उपसंख्यानम्': hṛda + yat (bhave chandasi, 4.4.110) with ay for the e ('hṛde + ya = hṛday + ya' in Vasu). The Kāśikā prints ह्रदय्या (hradayyā), the Kaumudī and the Mahābhāṣya hṛdayyā; I follow the Kaumudī. Vedic only. Split by me.
Second vārttika on 6.1.83 (Mahābhāṣya: 'शरस्य च हृदस्य चातोऽव्वक्तव्यः। हृदव्या आपः। शरव्या वै तेजनम्'): here it is av (not ay) and it replaces the final a. Vedic. Split by me.
'chandasīti kim?': in ordinary language the forms are bheyam / praveyam. Same letters as bhayyam; the difference is veda=false.
Ordinary language praveyam (Kāśikā).

k after r after the vowel a is doubled. 8.4.46 is optional (vā anuvṛtti from 8.4.45, Tattvabodhinī on 8.4.47: 'यरो वेति चानुवर्तते'); Śākalya (8.4.51) gives arkaḥ with no doubling. Input shows the pausal visarga form (arka + s).
Same as arkkaḥ.
m after h after the vowel a is doubled (optional). Śākalya/8.4.51: brahmā.
n after h (after the vowel a of apa) is doubled, although a vowel (u) follows: 8.4.46 doubles even before a vowel, unlike 8.4.47.

'aca iti kim?': the n is not after a vowel (the h follows the m/n of kim), so no doubling. The m before h + n becomes n or anusvāra by napare naḥ (8.3.27; Kāśikā on 8.3.27: 'किन् ह्नुते, किं ह्नुते'); the 8.4.46 passage prints the n form (with a space).
'aca iti kim?': the m is not after a vowel, no doubling. m before h + m is he mapare vā (8.3.26; Kāśikā on 8.3.26: 'किम् ह्मलयति किं ह्मलयति'): m stays or becomes anusvāra.

source.quote: acaḥ parābhyāṃ rephahakārābhyāṃ parasya yaro dve vā staḥ / gauryyau

notes: gaurī + au: yaṇ (6.1.77), then y after r after the vowel au is doubled (optional). 6.1.127 (Śākalya's hrasva alternative) does not apply because gaurī is not pada-final here (Laghu text on 6.1.127: 'padāntā iti kim ? gauryau').

Bālamanoramā: 'हरेरनुभवः: हरि-अनुभव इति स्थिते रेफादिकारस्य यण् । तस्य द्वित्वम्'. The y follows r (which follows the vowel a) and is followed by a vowel, so 8.4.47 anaci ca cannot apply but 8.4.46 can (Bālamanoramā: 'अचः परत्वाऽभावादच्परकत्वाच्च द्वित्वमप्राप्तं विधीयते').
y after h (after the vowel a) is doubled before the vowel a (Bālamanoramā: 'नहि — अस्ति इति स्थिते हकारादिकारस्य यण् । तस्य द्वित्वम्').

Laghu (corpus and GRETIL text): vārttika 'na samāse' with the example vāpyaśvaḥ - no doubling of the y in a compound. The Laghu attaches it to 8.4.46, but here the y stands after p, not after r/h, so the mechanism that would double it is not stated in the on-disk sources (probably the vārttika 'yaṇo mayo dve' of 8.4.47). Treat as an open point; do not implement doubling here.
'aca ity eva': the doubling only happens to a yar standing after a VOWEL. The m of smitam follows s, not a vowel: no doubling.
Same: m follows dh, not a vowel.

Vārttika 'यणो मयो द्वे भवत इति वक्तव्यम्', first reading (yaṇaḥ pañcamī, mayaḥ ṣaṣṭhī): a may (k) after a yaṇ (l) is doubled (Mahābhāṣya: 'यदि यण इति पञ्चमी मय इति षष्ठी उल्क्का वल्म्मीकमित्युदाहरणम्'). Optional (vā).
Same vārttika, first reading: m after l is doubled. (Vasu on this sūtra prints वाल्मीकः.)

Vārttika 'शरः खयो द्वे भवत इति वक्तव्यम्', first reading (śaraḥ pañcamī, khayaḥ ṣaṣṭhī): a khay (th) after a śar (s) is doubled. The Kāśikā writes the doubled aspirate as t + th (स्त्थाली = stthālī), the Mahābhāṣya as th + th (स्थ्थाली = sththālī); both spellings are listed. Optional (vā).
Same as sthālī (Kāśikā/Mahābhāṣya स्थ्थाता).

Vārttika 'śaraḥ khayo dve', second reading (khayaḥ pañcamī, śaraḥ ṣaṣṭhī): a śar (s) after a khay (t) is doubled -> vatssaḥ. vathsaḥ is the Pauṣkarasādi variant (vārttika 'चयो द्वितीयाः शरि पौष्करसादेः' under 8.4.48): a car before a śar becomes the aspirate of its class. Visarga = nominative -s.
Second reading: ṣ after k is doubled -> ikṣṣuḥ.
Second reading: ṣ after k doubled -> kṣṣīram; khṣīram is the Pauṣkarasādi variant (Kāśikā on 8.4.48: 'ककारस्य खकारः — ख्षीरम्').
Second reading: s after p doubled -> apssarāḥ; aphsarāḥ is the Pauṣkarasādi variant (Kāśikā on 8.4.48: 'पकारस्य फकारः — अफ्सराः').

Vārttika 'अवसाने च यरो द्वे भवत इति वक्तव्यम्': a yar at the pause is doubled (optional). Possible because 'anaci' is a paryudāsa (= 'other than a vowel', pause included; Mahābhāṣya: 'नायं प्रसज्यप्रतिषेधः - अचि नेति। किं तर्हि? पर्युदासोऽयं यदन्यदचेति'). Input is the pausal form.
Same vārttika (avasāne ca).
Same vārttika.
Same vārttika.

Laghu: 'saṃyogāntaṃ yatpadaṃ tadantasya lopaḥ syāt' + 1.1.52 alo 'ntyasya: 'iti yalope prāpte'; the y-deletion is prāpta but blocked by the vārttika 'yaṇaḥ pratiṣedho vācyaḥ'
Laghu: 'iti yalope prāpte - (yaṇaḥ pratiṣedho vācyaḥ) / suddhyupāsyaḥ'

source.quote: iti yalope prāpte - (yaṇaḥ pratiṣedho vācyaḥ) / suddhyupāsyaḥ

notes: Varadarāja's derivation of the compound sudhī-upāsya ('worshipped by the wise'; Bālamanoramā: 'सुधीभि रूपास्य इति विग्रहः', tṛtīyā-samāsa with bhis-luk). Steps as in the Laghu: (1) 6.1.77 with 1.1.66 (tasmin nirdiṣṭe pūrvasya: only the ī before the vowel is replaced) and 1.1.50 (sthāne 'ntaratamaḥ: ī -> y) gives 'sudhy upāsya'; (2) 8.4.47 anaci ca doubles the dh: 'sudhdhy upāsya'; (3) 8.4.53 changes the first dh to d: 'suddhy upāsya'; (4) 8.2.23 saṃyogāntasya lopaḥ (with 1.1.52 alo 'ntyasya) would now delete the final y ('iti yalope prāpte') - the vārttika 'yaṇaḥ pratiṣedho vācyaḥ' forbids it -> suddhyupāsyaḥ. The Mahābhāṣya (quoted by the Kāśikā) answers that no such word exists: 'काष्ठशगेव नास्ति कुतोऽयं काष्ठशकि तिष्ठेत्' - so the vārttika is rejected. Kept as an open point; do not implement.

source.quote: padānte jhali ca yaḥ saṃyogastadādyoḥ skorlopaḥ / bhṛṭ

notes: Laghu text vlk_311: bhṛsj (bhṛjjati, kvip) -> bhṛṭ. The Laghu gives only 8.2.29 for the step; the following ṣatva and ṭutva (8.2.36, 8.4.41) are not named. SK: 'भृट् । भृड्' (car/jaśtva option at the pause).
Laghu text: bhṛḍbhyām. Before the jhal bh the s of the conjunct sj is deleted by 8.2.29 (the ending starts with a jhal); the later ṣatva/ṭutva/jaśtva steps are not named. Input split by me.

Kāśikā: 'सवर्णप्रदेशाः — अकः सवर्णे दीर्घः इत्येवमादयः'. Both a's are savarṇa (same sthāna kaṇṭha, same prayatna), so 6.1.101 gives the long ā. The same example is used for 1.1.50 (sthānataḥ: the ā is kaṇṭhya).
Long ā + short a are savarṇa (18 varieties of a).

source.quote: akaḥ savarṇe 'ci pare pūrvaparayordīrgha ekādeśaḥ syāt / daityāraḥ / śrīśiḥ / viṣṇūdayaḥ / hotṝkāraḥ //

notes: Vārttika 'ṛḷvarṇayor mithaḥ sāvarṇyaṃ vācyam' (1.1.9; Kāśikā: 'होतृ ऌकारः — होतृृकारः'): ṛ and ḷ are savarṇa, so ṛ + ḷ -> long ṝ (no ḷ-dīrgha exists, Kāśikā: 'ऌवर्णस्य दीर्घा न सन्ति'). Source shown is the Laghu's example list under 6.1.101. The same list prints 'daityāraḥ' for daityāriḥ (SK) - a GRETIL corruption. Split by me.
'āsyagrahaṇaṃ kim?': p and t have the same prayatna but different sthāna, so they are NOT savarṇa and 8.4.65 (jharo jhari savarṇe) does not delete the p. Input tṛp + tā (guṇa ar) split by me.

'prayatnagrahaṇaṃ kim?': ś and c have the same sthāna (tālu) but different prayatna, so they are not savarṇa and 8.4.65 does not delete the ś. The ś itself is visarga-ścutva (8.3.34, 8.4.40; not named). Input written with the underlying s.
Tattvabodhinī's counter-example for 'prayatna': ś (ūṣman) and c (sparśa) are not savarṇa, so 8.4.65 does not delete the ś. Input shows the kutva-ed final k (from vāc).

a and h have the same sthāna and prayatna but an ac and a hal are never savarṇa (nāj-jhalau), so no savarṇa-dīrgha happens (there is no vowel following anyway; the point is 'ā + h' not being treated as savarṇa).
i and ś: the same sthāna (tālu) and, in the Kāśikā's view of prayatna, an ac and a hal are not savarṇa; so no dīrgha (and no yaṇ, because ś is not an ac).

source.quote: तेन दधीत्यस्य हरति शीतलं षष्ठं सान्द्रमित्येतेषु परेषु यणादिकं न

notes: SK/Laghu: if h were savarṇa to a (and so counted as an ac), dadhi + harati would get yaṇ; nājjhalau prevents it. Same for śītalam, ṣaṣṭham, sāndram.

source.quote: तेन दधीत्यस्य हरति शीतलं षष्ठं सान्द्रमित्येतेषु परेषु यणादिकं न

notes: ṛ-varṇa/ṣ savarṇa pair: no yaṇ before ṣ.
sthānataḥ āntaryam: of the possible long vowels the one with the same sthāna (kaṇṭhya ā) is the substitute (Kāśikā: 'द्वयोरकारयोः कण्ठ्य एव दीर्घ आकारो भवति').

Where several types of āntarya compete, sthāna wins ('यत्रानेकविधमान्तर्यं तत्र स्थानत आन्तर्यं बलीयः'): for i/u the guṇa e/o (same sthāna) and not a (same measure, pramāṇa). 7.3.84 is named in the Bālamanoramā on 1.1.50, not in the Kāśikā. tṛc has ṛ; the nominative gives cetā.
Same, u -> o.
guṇataḥ āntaryam: coḥ kuḥ (7.3.52) replaces c by the k of the same guṇa (voiceless, unaspirated), j by g. The vṛddhi ā (7.2.116) is not named here. Split by me.
j -> g (voiced, unaspirated); split by me.
pramāṇataḥ āntaryam: adaso 'ser dād u do maḥ (8.2.80) replaces the vowel after d by a short u for a short a and by long ū for a long one; the d becomes m. The ṣ of smai is ṣatva (not named).
Same: bhyām lengthens (dīrgha -> ū).
uraṇ raparaḥ: the a of guṇa which replaces ṛ is followed by r (a + r = ar). 7.3.84 is not named by the Kāśikā. Nominative of the tṛc form.
Same.
ṝta iddhātoḥ (7.1.100) gives i and 1.1.51 makes it ir (i + r). Root kṝ (kṝ vikṣepe) with śa; split by me.
Same (gṝ).

source.quote: ṛ iti triṃśataḥ saṃjñetyuktam / tatsthāne yo 'ṇ sa raparaḥ sanneva pravartate / kṛṣṇarddhiḥ / tavalkāraḥ //

notes: a + ṛ -> guṇa; the a-substitute is raparaḥ and by āntarya (ṛ is ṛ-sthāna) it is ar (SK: 'तत्रान्तरतम्यात् कृष्णर्द्धिरित्यत्राऽर्'). SK adds 'अचो रहाभ्याम् द्वे इति पक्षे द्वित्वम्' - an optional extra doubling of the dh after r; not enumerated here.

source.quote: ṛ iti triṃśataḥ saṃjñetyuktam / tatsthāne yo 'ṇ sa raparaḥ sanneva pravartate / kṛṣṇarddhiḥ / tavalkāraḥ //

notes: a + ḷ -> al (vārttika 'lapara iti vaktavyam' on 1.1.51: the substitute for ḷ is followed by l, so al).
id goṇyāḥ (1.2.50) is stated with a genitive (goṇyāḥ), so by alo 'ntyasya only the FINAL ī becomes short i. Split by me (dvigu, taddhitārtha).
Same as pañcagoṇiḥ.
ato bhisa ais (7.1.9): the a of 'ato' is tapara (a-t), so it refers only to SHORT a (same time), not to ā. Input carries the underlying -s of bhis; the output shows the visarga.
Same as vṛkṣaiḥ.
'tatkālasyeti kim?': without tatkāla, 7.1.9 would also apply to long ā and give khaṭvaiḥ; with it the ending stays -bhis (-bhiḥ).
Same as khaṭvābhiḥ.

Yathāsaṃkhya (1.3.10) example of the vārttika 'यवलपरे यवला वेति वक्तव्यम्' under he mapare vā (8.3.26; corpus.varttikas_on('8.3.26')): m before h + y/v/l becomes y/v/l respectively (kiy hyaḥ, kiv̐ hvalayati, kil hlādayati) or anusvāra. The printed Kāśikā shows the y/l forms with a private-use candrabindu glyph (U+F151) that cannot be quoted; SK on 1.3.10 lists the same words (कियूँह्यः । किंह्यः । किब्ँह्वलयति ...) with a candrabindu; the spellings with and without candrabindu (U+0310) are both listed.
